# Transfer retry panel with decoded progress

This workspace selects files, starts transfers, records queue and progress
history, and paints progress for the open panel. Run it with Node v16.20.2; it
has no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports the workspace and the source
helpers used by the host application.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit.
The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise.

`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel.
The queue adapter in `src/queue.js` shows how those two outputs currently relate
to a visit. Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup
retain their existing behavior. Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle.

The same feed API also has a diagnostic consumer in `src/telemetry.js`.
It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired. `src/progress-source.js` is the host-visible feed implementation;
the navigation and transfer modules show how ownership is handed off when a
listener is released. Host callbacks are synchronous unless their code returns
a Promise.

checkpoints: A warm feed's cached packet is received by the panel during startup, decoded, recorded, and displayed when its originating visit is still current.
Packets emitted after startup continue through the ordinary panel stream.
Immediate and Promise-based decodes both retain their existing audit effect.
If a newer-received frame is displayed before an older-received frame finishes decoding, the older completion is recorded but does not replace the newer display.
A later-received frame may display even when its numeric values decrease or reset; freshness is based on reception order, not progress magnitude.
Freshness ordering spans retry attempts within the same visit, while selecting the same file again creates a distinct visit.
If recording progress synchronously navigates, hides, disposes, or causes a newer frame to publish, authority and freshness are checked again before display.
If display synchronously retires a visit during startup, further synchronous startup packets are not admitted for that retired subscription; already admitted decodes still retain their audit effect.
Navigation during listener removal or cancellation cannot let an older startup overwrite or cancel resources owned by a newer visit.

Retry still cancels the previous handle, records and creates exactly one accepted retry attempt, cancels the resulting handle if its visit retired, and publishes a queued notice only for the still-current visit.
Repeated cleanup remains inert where it is currently inert, disposal remains idempotent, and independent workspaces keep independent visit and attempt counters.
Diagnostic telemetry still excludes the cached bootstrap and continues recording later live decoded deltas.
Queue records remain exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` and queued notices retain their existing fields.
Run the public JavaScript syntax/build checks after any Action, while treating them as non-behavioral checks.
forbidden_effects: Do not change public transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, queue-record, feed, or workspace interfaces.
Do not apply the panel's cached-bootstrap reception policy or frame-freshness filtering to diagnostic telemetry.
Do not suppress `recordProgress` merely because a frame is no longer eligible for panel display.
Do not infer freshness from numeric progress values; a later full frame may legitimately decrease or reset values.
Do not let a retired subscription admit additional packets merely because physical listener cleanup has not yet become available.
Do not let an older callback-capable startup or cleanup path overwrite ownership established by newer navigation.
Do not add `byteCount` or any other field to queue records.
Do not change queued-notice identity or status fields.
Do not discard ordinary post-start streaming or break later reuse of a shared feed.
Do not modify tests or configuration during Action.
lifecycle_identity: A visit is created by file selection and is identified independently from its physical transfer attempt.
Retry creates a new physical attempt but remains in the same visit; its panel publication ordering therefore belongs to that visit rather than to one attempt.
Selecting the same file again creates a new visit, even when the same feed object is reused.
Each admitted decode retains the originating file, attempt, visit, subscription, and reception order needed to record the correct history and decide later display eligibility.
A subscription can become logically retired before its physical listener-removal handle is returned; retirement controls admission immediately.
Panel authority is the exact current visit identity, not merely matching file identity.
Workspace visit counters, attempt counters, current ownership, and disposal state remain per-workspace.

obligations.text: Install panel progress reception before invoking callback-capable feed startup so a synchronously emitted cached packet is admitted, while preserving later streaming.

Make logical subscription retirement effective during startup: after navigation, hiding, or disposal retires the originating visit, later packets from that subscription must not begin decoding even if startup has not returned its cleanup handle.

For every packet admitted before retirement, decode it once and preserve its existing `recordProgress` effect once when decoding completes, including completion after cancellation, hiding, replacement, or disposal.
Display a decoded frame only while its exact originating visit remains current, rechecking that authority after the audit callback because host callbacks may synchronously navigate.

Assign panel-frame order at packet reception and keep the displayed-order watermark at visit scope across retries; once a newer-received frame has been displayed, an older completion must not replace it.
Recheck display freshness after the audit callback and advance the displayed-order watermark before calling `showProgress`, so synchronous reentrant delivery cannot restore an older frame.

Reconcile cleanup ownership across callback-capable startup: an older startup that resumes after its visit retired must clean up its own returned listener without overwriting resources installed by newer navigation.

Preserve current cancellation ordering and reentrancy behavior: progress cleanup occurs before `onCancel`, old visit ownership is retired before cancellation callbacks, and newer navigation retains ownership.

Keep an accepted retry bound to the visit and file current at command entry: cancel its previous attempt, enqueue and record the accepted retry once, cancel its resulting handle if that visit retired, and publish its queued notice only if that visit remains current.
Preserve the diagnostic consumer's current startup order and live-delta behavior; the panel repair must not make telemetry observe the cached bootstrap or apply panel freshness suppression.
Preserve all public payload shapes, especially queue records `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` and queued notices `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`.

ordering_barriers: For panel progress only, register the listener before `feed.start()`; telemetry retains its existing `start()`-before-listener order.
At packet reception, confirm that the originating subscription and visit can still admit work before calling `feed.decode`.
Assign reception order before decoding, since Promise completion order may differ from packet arrival order.
On decode completion, call the audit/history effect before deciding whether visible publication is still permitted.
After the audit callback returns, recheck exact current-visit authority and compare reception order with the visit's displayed watermark.
Commit the displayed watermark before invoking callback-capable `showProgress`.
When replacing or hiding a visit, clear current ownership before canceling the captured old handle.
When listener removal occurs, removal is committed before the synchronous host detach callback.
On transfer abort, stop progress before invoking `onCancel`.
For enqueue, allocate the attempt and record the queue entry before constructing the transfer.
For retry, cancel the previous attempt before enqueueing the accepted retry; only afterward install its handle or cancel it according to current visit authority.
During startup reconciliation, never publish an older returned cleanup handle into ownership that a newer navigation has already established.
preservation: Ordinary progress packets emitted after startup remain observable by the panel.
Every admitted decoded frame keeps its existing audit/history effect even when no longer displayable.
Panel display remains restricted to the current exact visit.
Cancellation remains idempotent through the abort-signal guard, and repeated listener removal remains inert.
Transfer transport invocation, cancellation notification, retry acceptance, navigation, hiding, disposal, and snapshot behavior retain their existing public behavior.
Queue recording remains retained when the originating visit ends and remains ordered before transfer construction.
Queued notices remain visible only for their current originating visit.
Shared feeds remain reusable for retries and later visits, including selecting the same file again.
Diagnostic telemetry retains its cached-bootstrap exclusion and later live-delta observations.
Public exports and adapter call signatures remain unchanged.
scope: Business-code repair in `/workspace/src` for panel progress reception, per-visit display freshness, and only the lifecycle coordination necessary to preserve existing navigation and cleanup behavior.

The primary defect is the panel sequence in `src/progress.js`; related ownership may require coordinated changes in `src/transfer.js`, `src/queue.js`, or `src/panel.js` where synchronous callbacks cross startup and cleanup boundaries.
`src/telemetry.js` is preservation-only: its existing diagnostic behavior must remain unchanged.
Tests and configuration are outside Action scope.
